title: Docs contributor workflow: SDK examples, snippet hygiene, and emergency hotfix playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This page defines the canonical contributor workflow and operational playbook for authoring and shipping SDK examples, documentation code snippets, and fast emergency hotfixes to the docs site. It covers: ownership, CI gating, snippet hygiene, telemetry links to support cases, rollback steps, and a compact ‘canonical fix’ template everyone should use when addressing frequent support issues. The intent is to reduce flaky examples in customer-facing docs, shorten time-to-first-fix, and make postmortems actionable.

When to use this playbook

- New SDK examples or sample apps that will be embedded on docs-site.
- Any change to code snippets in the snippet-registry that affects more than one SDK language.
- Hotfixes for docs that cause customer-facing regressions (build failures, incorrect authentication examples, out-of-date API shapes).
- Emergency removals of snippets flagged by support or security.

Service names and tooling referenced

- docs-site: the static site front-end and renderer (internal repo: docs.redwood.dev).
- dx-snippet-builder: microservice that extracts, compiles, and runs code snippets from markdown.
- snippet-registry: canonical source-of-truth for all published snippets (git-submodule).
- docs-ci: CI pipeline that validates builds, snippet tests, and style checks.
- telemetry-ingest: central telemetry collector; links to support-case-tracker when docs changes correlate with errors.
- support-case-tracker: Zendesk/linear integration used by support to raise doc-related incidents.

SLOs and quality gates

- docs-site build time: median <= 8 minutes, 95th percentile <= 15 minutes.
- snippet test pass rate: >= 98% on main branch before release.
- Example runtimes: unit/compile smoke tests must run in < 30s per example.
- Hotfix turnaround SLA: first triage within 1 hour, patch deployed to staging within 3 hours, production rollback or patch within 6 hours.

Roles & ownership

- Author: contributor who opens PR containing code snippet or doc text. Responsible for the initial patch and verifying local tests.
- Reviewer: a peer with SDK familiarity (at least one engineer from SDK team). Must verify snippet correctness in two languages when applicable.
- Docs Release Manager: rotates weekly; approves deploy to production and coordinates hotfixes.
- On-call Docs Engineer: 24/7 pager for production docs regressions. Executes emergency rollback/runbook if needed.

Contributor workflow (standard change)

1) Authoring
   - Create a local feature branch in docs-site repo and update snippet-registry if adding or editing code.
   - Run dx-snippet-builder locally: `yarn run dx-snippet:build --watch` to validate extractions.
   - Add a short description and test matrix to the snippet file header (see Template section).

2) Pre-PR checks (local)
   - `scripts/run-snippet-smoke.sh` (runs all altered snippets with language matrix).
   - `yarn lint:md` and `yarn lint:samples`.
   - Update the PR body with the canonical fix template (copy from Appendix).

3) CI validation (docs-ci)
   - docs-ci runs: doc build, snippet compilation, snippet unit tests, accessibility checks, link-checker, and content spellcheck.
   - Failing snippet tests block merge; notify reviewer and add label `docs:needs-snippet-fix`.

4) Review and merge
   - Reviewer confirms code accuracy and that snippets demonstrate recommended best-practices (idempotent auth, safe defaults, no hardcoded secrets).
   - Squash-merge after approval. Ensure commit message references issue or support case (if applicable).

5) Post-merge verification
   - Docs CI deploys to `staging.docs.redwood.dev`. Author or Release Manager must smoke test examples on staging within 30 minutes.

Authoring checklist (quick)

- Does snippet have a header with language, required deps, and CLI to run?
- Are credentials redacted or use environment variables with examples?
- Is there a one-paragraph explanation above the snippet describing intent and failure modes?
- Are output examples reproducible and bounded (e.g., deterministic seeds)?
- Does it use recommended SDK pattern (retry/backoff, streaming fallback) per SDK guidelines?

Canonical fix template (copy into PR body)

- Problem summary: one-line.
- Impact: number of pages, customer-visible examples, support cases referenced.
- Root cause (short): e.g., API shape change, bad copy-paste, deprecated parameter.
- Fix performed: files changed, snippet-registry entries modified.
- Tests added: smoke + language matrix.
- Rollout plan: staging verification steps, target release.

Emergency hotfix procedure

1) Triage (first 60 minutes)
   - On-call engineers triage the report in support-case-tracker. Classify severity: P0 (site broken/compile failure), P1 (misleading auth sample), P2 (typo/non-critical).
   - If P0/P1, create a hotfix branch named `hotfix/docs/<short-desc>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>`.

2) Patch & PR
   - Minimal change only: update or remove offending snippet. When in doubt, remove snippet and add a temporary warning banner using the docs-site banner macro.
   - Run `scripts/run-snippet-smoke.sh --quick` and open PR flagged with labels `hotfix` and `urgent`.

3) Review & fast-merge
   - One reviewer required for content; Docs Release Manager must approve deployment bypass if necessary.
   - Use CI override only when on-call explicitly documents why (examples: time-to-fix > 4 hours, docs build blocked by unrelated flaky test). Overrides are recorded in PR comments.

4) Staging deploy & verification
   - Deploy to staging and execute the staging verification checklist (see Appendix). Notify support that fix is in staging and request confirmation.

5) Production deploy
   - After staging sign-off, Release Manager triggers production deploy. Confirm with support and close related support case.

Rollback steps (if production regression detected)

- Immediate action: Revert the merge commit and re-deploy via `docs-ci` revert job. This is preferred for content regressions.
- If revert fails, enable the docs-site maintenance banner and disable snippet rendering by flipping `SNIPPETS_ENABLED=false` in runtime config via the console.
- Post-incident: open postmortem and tag `docs-hotfix` with timeline and RCA.

Telemetry and support linkages

- All doc PRs that change executable snippets must include the snippet id. dx-snippet-builder attaches a `snippet_id` to telemetry events.
- When support files a case referencing a snippet, include `snippet_id` to make triage fast. Telemetry queries: `select count(*) from telemetry_ingest where snippet_id = '<id>' and error = true` helps find correlated errors.

Docs site release schedule and gating

- Weekly cadence for non-urgent content releases: merges to `main` are deployed on Tuesday at 10:00 PT after CI passes.
- Hotfixes are deployed immediately after verification.
- Monthly snippet-registry clean-up: remove deprecated snippets older than 18 months after owner approval.

Examples

- Example snippet header (add at top of code block):
```
# snippet_id: rx-sdk-auth-202402
# languages: python, javascript
# deps: redwood-sdk>=1.3.0
# smoke: python -m examples.rx_auth_test
```

- Local smoke run (bash):
```
./scripts/run-snippet-smoke.sh files/paths/changed --languages python,js --timeout 30
```

- Minimal PR checklist comment to paste into your PR: 
```
Summary: Fix outdated auth example in `getting-started/auth.md`
Impact: Affects 3 pages and 2 SDK examples; 4 related support cases (#1234-1237)
Root cause: API signature changed in SDK v1.3.0
Fix: Updated python/js snippets and smoke tests.
Tests: smoke + unit coverage for snippets added.
Rollout: staged -> verified -> prod deploy.
```

Appendix: staging verification checklist

- Confirm docs build passes and staging deploy completes within 15 minutes.
- Manually run altered snippets in staging environment with `SNIPPET_MODE=staging`.
- Validate that no links or anchor tags are broken for updated pages.
- Confirm with the support rep who reported the issue.

Appendix: sample PR body template (copyable)

- Title: `[docs] Fix: <short description>`
- Body:
  - Problem summary:
  - Files changed:
  - Snippet IDs affected:
  - Test matrix run:
  - Staging verification steps performed:
  - Release manager approval (name):

Appendix: governance notes

- Any change that touches three or more pages must include a cross-team reviewer from Developer Experience and SDK.
- Deleting a snippet requires a migration note and a 14-day deprecation notice unless it is a security or correctness hotfix.
- Docs Release Manager rotates weekly. The rotation schedule and on-call runbook live at `/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/release-rotation`.

Contact and escalation

- Primary contact: docs-release@redwood.dev
- On-call: see PagerDuty schedule (docs-site-oncall)
- Support triage channel: #support-docs on Slack

This playbook should be reviewed quarterly. For questions or suggested updates, open a PR against this page or ping the Docs Release Manager.
